explanation: Count set bits separately in all 32 positions, then take each count modulo three. Triplicated numbers contribute multiples of three in every position, leaving exactly the singleton’s signed 32-bit representation.
timeComplexity: O(32n)=O(n) time: inspect every bit of each input, then reconstruct 32 result bits. Bitmask variants update two words per input; bit-count variants inspect a fixed 32 bits.
spaceComplexity: O(32)=O(1) auxiliary counters for the fixed 32-bit input domain. Either two masks or 32 counters are fixed-size state.
attribution: Unmodified reference source: epi_judge_cpp_solutions/element_appearing_once.cc. Elements of Programming Interviews Judge authors; repository LICENSE: Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivatives 4.0 International. Explanation authored for EPI Practice.
correctness: For each bit position, all triplicated inputs contribute a multiple of three. Its count modulo three is therefore precisely the singleton’s bit at that position. Reassembling all 32 bits recovers the unique value; Python explicitly subtracts 2^32 when the sign bit is set.
walkthrough: In [−4,6,6,6,9,9,9], each set bit contributed by 6 or 9 occurs three times and cancels. The remaining signed bit pattern is −4.
edgeCases: The unique integer may be negative.
Zero may be the unique integer.
The contract gives every other integer exactly three occurrences.
